by: Claude (lead dev); independent review of the findings, 2026-10-22; independent review of the corrected text, 2026-10-22; re-check of six sentences revised after it, 2026-10-22. Derrida checked against the essay itself (Writing and Difference, trans. Bass, Routledge 2001, p. 357); Barthes and Kristeva against Blackburn, Oxford Dictionary of Philosophy, 2nd edn (2005).

mechanical.note: The article cites SEP 'Structuralism' (plato.stanford.edu/entries/structuralism/); SEP has no such entry (structuralism in mathematics and in physics only). The encyclopedia.com page could not be fetched from here.
Reviewer: Angermuller, Why There Is No Poststructuralism in France (Bloomsbury, 2015): the label belongs to the Anglophone world; in France there is no such category.
SEP Derrida (Lawlor) and SEP Foucault (Oksala) are cited without authors.

sentences.text: Structuralism explained meaning through systems of relations.

claims.excerpt: our world consists not of things but of relations

sentences.text: Saussure's Course in General Linguistics (1916), compiled from students' notes of his lectures, treated language as a system of signs whose elements have value only through their differences, and Lévi-Strauss in anthropology, Barthes in cultural criticism and Lacan in psychoanalysis, who held that the unconscious is structured like a language, carried the model into their fields.

claims.by: Saussure, Writings in General Linguistics (OUP 2006), abstract
claims.excerpt: posthumously composed by his students from the notes

claims.claim: the model carried into anthropology, psychoanalysis, literary theory
claims.by: Concise REP (2000) 'Post-structuralism in the social sciences' (Gutting)
claims.excerpt: later adapted in anthropology (by Lévi-Strauss), in psychoanalysis (by Lacan)
the unconscious is structured like a language

sentences.text: Ferdinand de Saussure distinguished the signifier and signified and emphasized that linguistic values arise from relations within a system rather than from simple labels attached to independently fixed concepts.

claims.excerpt: what counts are the relations, the contrasts, that differentiate signs
claims.note: Contrastive construction.
claims.fix: reword positively

sentences.text: The posthumously assembled Course in General Linguistics has a complex editorial history, and later scholars debate how faithfully it represents his lectures and manuscripts.

claims.by: Zhou, 'Saussure: Langue as an Autonomous System' (Springer, 2020), abstract
claims.excerpt: taken to be the best collection of Saussurean thought
claims.note: Saussure's own manuscripts, found in 1996, were compared with the 1916 Course by Bouquet and Engler (2002). 'Debate' is a fair summary but the abstract stops before their findings.
claims.fix: cite Zhou; say the 1996 manuscripts reopened the question

sentences.text: Structural approaches also differ in how they understand historical change and the role of speakers.

claims.by: Concise REP (2000) 'Saussure' (Holdcroft); SEP Philosophy of Linguistics §2
claims.note: Reviewer: Holdcroft gives only the priority of the synchronic system; nothing says structural approaches differ on change or speakers.
claims.fix: cut, or keep only Saussure's priority of the system at a time

sentences.text: Claude Lévi-Strauss examined kinship, classification, and myth through patterned relations and transformations, seeking structures that were not necessarily available to participants' conscious awareness.

claims.by: Concise REP (2000) 'Lévi-Strauss' (Olivia Harris); 'Post-structuralism in the social sciences' (Gutting)
claims.excerpt: meanings were constituted not by conscious subjects but by relations
claims.note: Kinship, classification and myth are standard but neither short entry lists them.

sentences.text: His work transformed anthropology while prompting disputes about historical specificity, colonial research settings, and the danger of reducing lived practices to formal oppositions.

claims.note: Reviewer agrees: no scholarly source lists those criticisms; Harkin (Cambridge Companion to Lévi-Strauss, 2009) notes only problems in imagining a structuralist history.
claims.fix: cut the list of criticisms, or replace with what Harris says structuralism set aside: the subject, metaphysics, continuity

sentences.text: Jacques Lacan reinterpreted Freud through linguistics and theories of the symbolic, imaginary, and real, while Roland Barthes analyzed the cultural work of signs in advertising, fashion, and everyday myths.

sentences.text: The French thinkers who came after, Derrida, Foucault, Deleuze and Lyotard among them, are often called post-structuralists because they worked with concepts developed in the structuralist revolution in Paris in the 1950s and early 1960s while questioning fixed structures, origins and the unified subject; many cite May 1968 as a turning point.

claims.excerpt: the structuralist revolution in Paris in the 1950s and early 1960s
claims.note: Reviewer: nearly the whole phrase is Aylesworth's ("concepts developed during the structuralist revolution in Paris in the 1950s and early 1960s"; May 1968 "a watershed moment").
claims.fix: credit Aylesworth and quote his phrase

sentences.text: Derrida's différance names a play of differences in which no meaning is ever simply present, and his “Structure, Sign, and Play” (1966) took Lévi-Strauss as its main subject.

claims.excerpt: a wandering play of differences
claims.note: Reviewer: Lawlor's passage concerns experience, not meaning; Aylesworth §5 supports "play of differences".

claims.claim: Structure, Sign, and Play took Lévi-Strauss as its main subject
claims.note: The essay discusses the history of structure (pp. 351–56), then Lévi-Strauss from p. 357 to the end, about 71% of its body. "Main subject" was overstated; "main example" is Derrida's own framing.
claims.fix: quote Derrida and cite p. 357
claims.by: Derrida, Writing and Difference, trans. Bass (Routledge, 2001), p. 357; SEP Hermeneutics §6.2
claims.excerpt: as an example, the texts of Claude Lévi-Strauss
